subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named hosting profiles as a stable readiness contract, and if so should acceptance initially cover only the local readiness foundation or all five proposed profiles?
rationale: The choice creates permanent public configuration, health, status, probe, and release-conformance obligations; implementation quality alone cannot determine whether maintainers want core to own that support boundary.

options.title: Accept Local Foundation
options.body: Approve the canonical condition model and default local projection first, then evaluate each non-local profile with operational and upgrade evidence.

options.title: Accept Full Catalog
options.body: Approve all five profiles and their selection and failure semantics as one stable core contract.

options.title: Keep Checks Host-Owned
options.body: Decline named core profiles and retain topology-specific conformance checks in hosting integrations or supervisors.

recommendation.title: Accept Local Foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the canonical condition model and default local projection first, then evaluate each non-local profile with operational and upgrade evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history established the RFC lifecycle used to route this product-scope and acceptance decision.
